scholarships.title: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
scholarships.degree: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
scholarships.official_source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS), administered with the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE)

existing.funding_period: monthly living stipend over an eleven-month fellowship
existing.description: The AEF Programme places accomplished K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, working on national education programmes and policy. Each fellow receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200, a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency, an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses, relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for fellows relocating from outside the Washington, DC area, and a health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month on an individual plan or $1,300 per month on a family plan. The DOE sponsors up to five congressional office placements. The programme is a single eleven-month appointment; it is not a degree award and involves no tuition.
eligibility: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).

Have a minimum of five complete years of full-time classroom teaching experience prior to submitting the application; student teaching does not count toward this minimum full-time teaching requirement.

Have been teaching full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school for at least five of the last seven years in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) discipline; current employment may be as an educator or district official.
Be currently employed full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school or school district in the U.S.
Be able to provide a letter of recommendation from a school district official as one of their three required letters of recommendation.
Be able to obtain a leave of absence from teaching in order to participate in the program for the full eleven months.
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens who have completed five years of full-time STEM classroom teaching, have taught full-time in a U.S. public or private elementary or secondary school or school district for at least five of the last seven years, are currently so employed, can obtain an eleven-month leave of absence, and can obtain a recommendation letter from a school district official.
benefits: Develops a professional development plan to guide individual professional development objectives outside host office responsibilities, with ongoing mentoring provided by the AEF Programme.
Access to a national network of education leaders and programmes.
Placement in a federal agency or U.S. Congressional office, with the DOE sponsoring up to five placements in congressional offices.
Up to ten personal days off per year and up to ten sick days off without reduction in the Fellow's stipend.
Fellows are connected with outgoing Fellows to help identify available housing in the Washington, DC area.
coverage: Travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency; limitations on foreign travel vary by agency.
Education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved expenses aligned with the Fellow's individual professional development plan, including courses, conferences and professional books.
Relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for Fellows relocating from outside of the Washington, DC area (home-to-Washington distance more than 50 miles one way).
Stipend of up to $550 per month (individual plan) or $1,300 per month (family plan) to offset the cost of health insurance.
Designated office space and agency/office-specific orientation and training.
Official twice monthly professional development meetings, conferences and field trips organised for Fellows by the AEF Programme.
requirements: All applications must be completed online through the online application system.
Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements.
All applications, including recommendations, are due by the specified application deadline; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for evaluation and placement.
Materials uploaded into the application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Completion of all required fields, including contact information; education background (formal education and continuing education); teaching and professional experience; professional awards and recognition; citizenship status; interest in federal agency and/or Congressional office placement; and five essay questions.
Submission of three letters of recommendation online, including one recommendation letter from a school district official.
School district officials do not include department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals or vice-principals.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring their recommenders have the information needed to access the online Recommender form; requests can only be sent electronically through the online application system.
Provide proof of U.S. citizenship upon accepting a Fellowship offer.
Secure a leave of absence from teaching during the fellowship year.
Complete the eleven-month full-time appointment (mid-August through mid-July) in Washington, DC.
Meet the terms and conditions in the offer letter of appointment, including requirements for ethical conduct, and financial disclosure and conflict of interest.
Participate in the official professional development meetings, conferences and field trips organised for Fellows by the AEF Programme.
Have health care coverage during the fellowship appointment; Fellows are eligible to participate in the ORISE health insurance plan if they do not have other health insurance coverage.
Establish an individual Professional Development Plan for the year, which must be completed by early October.
Submit the requested written reports, presentations and surveys related to the Fellowship experience before the published deadlines.
Represent themselves as educators in a responsible and professional manner.
Only use the AEF Programme name or the Fellow's affiliation with the AEF Programme in an authorised manner.
In managing their responsibilities throughout the fellowship, give priority to the duties assigned to them by their host office.
documents: Completed online application with all required fields (contact information, education background, teaching and professional experience, professional awards and recognition, citizenship status, interest in federal agency and/or Congressional office placement).
Three letters of recommendation submitted online, one of which must be from a school district official.
application_method: Create a new User ID and Password in the online application system (click 'Create New Account').
Complete all required fields of the online application.
Draft the five essay responses offline in word processing software, spell-check them, and copy and paste into the appropriate areas of the online application.

Request recommendations from three individuals familiar with the applicant's professional and education background and their experience, aptitude or promise relevant to the AEF Programme, entering their names and email addresses on the Request Recommendations page; requests can be made as soon as the application system is accessed, without waiting for the application to be complete.

Confirm that one recommender is a school district official and select the correct Type option (a school headmaster/headmistress or equivalent to a school principal qualifies; choose 'Other' and enter the position title in the Other District Official text box).
Monitor the 'Check Your Status' page to confirm that all three recommendations have been submitted; use the 'Resend Email' button on the Recommendations tab to chase recommenders.
Submit the completed application, including all three letters of recommendation, by 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026.
Check Your Status periodically before the deadline; the applicant is responsible for confirming completeness, as the programme will not tell them what is missing.
If selected as a semi-finalist, travel to Washington, DC on Saturday February 27, 2027, attend orientation on Sunday February 28, and be interviewed Monday March 1 and possibly Tuesday March 2.
Finalists selected for a Congressional office placement return to Washington, DC in mid-June 2027 for a week of placement interviews.
existing.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.
existing.best_fit: Experienced, currently employed U.S. K-12 STEM teachers or district officials who have at least five complete years of full-time classroom STEM teaching, can secure an eleven-month leave of absence, and can relocate to the Washington, DC area.
existing.notes: Not deferrable and not renewable: the fellowship is for a single eleven-month period from mid-August with initial programme Orientation, and there is no flexibility in start and end dates. There is no return-home requirement, but relocation to the Washington, DC area is a programme requirement if the Fellow does not already live there. The Fellow cannot maintain a teaching position while serving; a leave of absence must be secured or employment terminated. The AEF Programme does not arrange housing. Fellows receive a monthly stipend and are not considered employees of the hosting office, so they do not earn sick or annual leave, although up to ten personal days and ten sick days are allowed without stipend reduction. All stipends are reportable to the Internal Revenue Service and the AEF Programme does not withhold taxes; fellows may need to file Form 1040-ES and pay estimated income tax. Current and former AEF Fellows are not eligible to apply for a second fellowship. No clinical restriction is published.
existing.duration: Eleven months, mid-August through mid-July; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial programme Orientation
existing.application_period: Online application opens August 3, 2026 and closes 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026 for the 2027-2028 programme. Semi-finalist notifications with travel arrangements are made by February 24, 2027; interviews in Washington, DC February 27 - March 1, 2027; finalist notifications March 9, 2027; congressional fellows placement interviews mid-June 2027; fellows arrive in Washington, DC mid-August 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.

scholarships.title: Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) Program
scholarships.official_source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS), administered with Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE)

existing.description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution. The award does not pay tuition or fees, does not cover supplies and materials, and does not cover travel during the project; the student must remain enrolled full-time at their home institution and keep paying their own tuition. Successful applicants are considered guest scientists at the host laboratory, not employees.
eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents aged 18 or older, full-time enrolled in a qualified thesis-based Ph.D. programme in a DOE-supported STEM field, have obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, and secure a collaborating scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory.
benefits: Access to DOE national laboratory expertise, user facilities, instrumentation and leadership-class computing systems.
Professional network expansion and access to scientific user facilities not available at most universities.
The possible opportunity for a short international research visit of 6 weeks maximum to an institution such as CERN or RIKEN, applied for after the award is received.
Weekly virtual office hours and application assistance workshops offered by the SCGSR Program.
A running list of collaborating laboratory scientists who are ready to work with SCGSR awardees.
coverage: A monthly stipend in the amount of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period.

Reimbursement for in-bound and out-bound transportation to the host DOE laboratory/facility, limited to a total travel benefit of up to $3,000 per award, available only if the host DOE national laboratory/facility is greater than 50 miles from the awardee's home graduate institution.
The opportunity, after receiving the award, to apply for further funding to conduct a brief (6 weeks maximum) research visit to select research institutions abroad, such as CERN or RIKEN.
requirements: All applications must be completed through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.
Materials uploaded into the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Complete all required fields: Contact Information; Academic Information including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed by the applicant and the collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, as a PDF through the online application.
Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts.
Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department.
Submit two Letters of Support, one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, both completed through the online application system.
Indicate in the online application system which Office of Science priority research area the proposed project aligns with.
List citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, in the appropriate section of the online application; do not submit supplemental materials.

The research proposal must address the stated aims in at least one of the SCGSR Priority Research Areas and must identify how the proposed research will take advantage of the DOE laboratory/facility's research capabilities and assets.

The proposed research must be an integral part of the applicant's overall doctoral thesis project and must be approved by the primary graduate thesis advisor, whose approval is made through the thesis advisor's Letter of Support.
Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline and become familiar with the application information requested.
documents: Completed online application with all required fields (contact information; academic information including current graduate program information; citizenship or permanent residency status; professional information including scientific publications and awards; graduate thesis advisor and collaborating DOE laboratory scientist contact information).
SCGSR research proposal as a PDF file, limited to three pages excluding references, with references on a separate page not exceeding one page.
Official graduate transcripts uploaded as a PDF, with all Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth redacted or removed but the applicant's name retained.

Official proof of Ph.D. candidacy: an official, signed letter from the applicant's university/college Registrar's office, or an official, signed letter from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department.
Letter of Support from the applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor, submitted through the online system.
Letter of Support from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, submitted through the online system.
Citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, entered in the online application sections.
application_method: Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline.
Review the eligibility rules, priority research areas and merit review criteria before writing anything.

Identify a collaborating research scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory or facility, or ask the SCGSR Program Manager or the laboratory point of contact for candidates, and agree the project scope with them.
Consult your primary graduate thesis advisor and confirm Ph.D. candidacy, an approved thesis topic, and that the proposed laboratory work is part of your thesis project.
Obtain official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as a signed letter from the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, including the date of thesis committee approval of your topic.
Obtain your official graduate transcript stamped with the university seal, and redact Social Security numbers and dates of birth while keeping your name visible.

Co-develop the research proposal with the collaborating scientist, in consultation with your thesis advisor, addressing the stated aims of at least one priority research area and identifying how the laboratory's capabilities and assets will be used; keep it to three pages plus a one-page reference list.

Ensure both your thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist review and approve the final proposal PDF before uploading it, because they receive an automatic notification when you upload or update it.

Enter your thesis advisor's contact information under 'Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor Information' and the collaborating scientist's contact information under 'Host DOE Laboratory', then use 'Send Email' on the Request Letters of Support tab to send both requests.
Monitor the receipt of both letters of support through the online system and send reminder emails where needed.
Review and print or export your application as a PDF using the 'Print your Application' option before submitting.

Submit the complete application, including transcripts, proof of candidacy, research proposal and both letters of support, by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026, and confirm the Status page shows 'Submitted'.
If selected, respond to the DOE Office of Science notification promptly; you will be given about a week to decide whether to accept.
existing.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.
existing.best_fit: Full-time U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents who have already obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, are enrolled in a thesis-based research Ph.D. in a DOE-supported STEM field at an accredited U.S. institution, and can arrange a 3 to 12 month in-person research residency with a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist at a participating laboratory.
existing.notes: Not deferrable in the ordinary sense, but the award period may be changed under exceptional circumstances, such as unexpected schedule changes at scientific user facilities, with the support of both the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist and the primary graduate thesis advisor; such requests must reach the SCGSR Program Manager at least 20 business days in advance with signed consent letters from both, and the overall project period must remain the same length as proposed. Cumulative SCGSR award periods across all awards may not exceed 12 months. The award is not an internship and not a full graduate fellowship: the SCGF programme, which provided a stipend and tuition support for up to three years, is no longer accepting applications. Awardees are not employees of the host laboratory or DOE and are not entitled to employee benefits. Regular travel between the host laboratory and the university during the award period violates the terms and conditions, because a full-time schedule at the host is required during normal laboratory business hours; awardees may observe the host's holidays but must report any expected interruption to the collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager. Awardees become ineligible if, after applying, they accept a separate non-SCGSR appointment from the host laboratory, such as an hourly paid intern or a full-time or temporary position. Medical research, or biological research on model systems for the purpose of understanding disease or pathogens, is not eligible, which excludes clinical and medical-degree routes; joint MD/PhD, joint JD/PhD, DVM, MBA, MD, JD and joint BS/MS programmes are all ineligible. Published work based on the research should carry the SCGSR acknowledgement statement, including contract number DE-SC0014664.
existing.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates
existing.application_period: 2026 Solicitation 2: online application opened August 12, 2026 and closes 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026. Offer notifications April 1 - 16, 2027. Proposed project periods may start as early as June 7, 2027 and must start no later than October 4, 2027. 2027 Solicitation 1 (tentative): application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027, offers September 2027, project periods starting November 2027 and ending no later than March 2028.
existing.deadline_display: Applications are due November 4, 2026, at 5:00PM ET. This is 2026 Solicitation 2. The online application system closes at 5:00 PM Eastern Time and no additional materials will be accepted after it. 2027 Solicitation 1 dates are published but all tentative: application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027.
